prose.favour: The case in its favour rests mostly on growth: profit grew 99% compared with a year earlier. Also in its favour: sales grew 23% compared with a year earlier; the share price is 36.3% higher than a year ago; and over the past year the share did 38.6 percentage points better than the Nifty 50. Other areas on this side: the recent price trend, what the price asks for the earnings, what the price implies.
prose.against: The case against rests mostly on cash flow and the balance sheet: return on capital employed is only 7.9%, a weak return on the money in the business. Also against it: net debt is 3.7 times a year of operating earnings, heavy; operating profit covers interest only 1.5 times, thin; and profit shrank 69.1% a year on average over three years. Other areas on this side: the balance sheet, price behaviour, the quality of the business.
prose.weighing: Weighing them: 7 points in favour and 11 against give more points against. The pool score is 45 of 100. The side that carries most weight is cash flow and the balance sheet. That gives an educational rating of Underweight with medium confidence. This is a rule-based reading of the evidence above, not a prediction.
